# How-to: Bridge USDC and EURC with CCTP - Arc Docs

Exchanges

Move USDC and EURC to and from Arc using Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol for exchange hot wallet funding and liquidity rebalancing.

[Circle’s Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP)](https://developers.circle.com/cctp) uses a burn-and-mint model to natively transfer USDC and EURC between blockchains without wrapped or bridged token variants. Arc’s CCTP domain is `26`. Transfers into Arc mint tokens directly to your recipient address; transfers out burn tokens on Arc and mint on the destination blockchain. Because Arc has [deterministic finality](/arc/concepts/deterministic-finality), outbound transfers reach attestation faster than transfers from blockchains that require multiple confirmations.

Before you begin, ensure that you’ve:

*   Obtained an RPC endpoint for Arc Testnet (`https://rpc.testnet.arc.io`)
*   Obtained an RPC endpoint for the source or destination blockchain (for example, Ethereum Sepolia)
*   Acquired a USDC or EURC balance on the sending blockchain
*   Reviewed the [CCTP developer docs](https://developers.circle.com/stablecoins/cctp-getting-started)
*   Installed `viem` in your TypeScript environment

## Short answer

On Arc there's no separate gas token to buy — **USDC is both the asset and the gas token**. So "funding your wallet" just means getting USDC onto Arc. There is **no mainnet faucet** (`faucet.circle.com` is testnet only). You fund it by withdrawing or bridging USDC in.

Arc mainnet parameters (from [docs.arc.io/arc/references/connect-to-arc](https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/connect-to-arc)):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Network name | Arc |
| RPC | `https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io` |
| Chain ID | `5042` |
| Currency symbol | USDC |
| Explorer | `https://explorer.arc.io` |

Arc's CCTP domain is `26`. Native balance/`eth_getBalance` uses **18 decimals**; the ERC-20 USDC interface uses **6 decimals** — same underlying asset, one row in your wallet.

## Three ways to fund it

**1. Withdraw from an exchange directly to Arc (easiest if supported)**
Open your exchange's USDC withdraw flow and pick **Arc / Arc Mainnet** in the network dropdown, then paste your Arc address. Robinhood and KuCoin announced direct USDC deposit/withdraw support on Arc at launch; BitGo added wallet/custody support day one. Check your own exchange's dropdown — if Arc isn't listed, use route 2.

**2. Bridge via Circle's CCTP (burn-and-mint, native USDC)**
This is the canonical path and gives you real USDC, not a wrapped IOU. Two options:
- **[portal.arc.io](https://portal.arc.io/)** — Circle's official front end; deposit from Ethereum/other supported chains, swap, send, all in one place.
- **CCTP directly / Bridge Kit** — if you're a developer or using a CCTP-aware bridge UI; see [docs.arc.io/integrate/exchanges/cctp-bridging](https://docs.arc.io/integrate/exchanges/cctp-bridging). Inbound flow: approve USDC → `depositForBurn` targeting domain 26 → wait for attestation → `receiveMessage` on Arc mints to your address.

**3. Third-party bridge routers** (Zerion Bridge, Relay-style aggregators) — fine, but compare fees and confirm the output is native USDC on Arc, not a wrapped variant.

## Wallet setup tips

- Add Arc with the table above; in MetaMask/Rabby you can also use the one-click "Add Arc Mainnet" button in the docs.
- You'll see **one USDC balance**. Don't import the ERC-20 USDC contract *as a second token* — it's the same asset and will double-count.
- Register `nativeCurrency.decimals = 18` when adding the chain, but display balances to 6 decimals. Some wallets show fees as "ETH/Gwei" on Arc — that's a mislabel; fees are USDC.
- You need a nonzero USDC balance before you can do anything, since gas is paid in USDC. Bridging in solves both at once.

## Cautions

- Lots of "how to bridge to Arc" pages are airdrop-farming SEO content. Use **portal.arc.io**, **docs.arc.io**, or your exchange. Never enter a seed phrase into a bridge site — bridges only ever need your public address.
- Minimum bridge/withdrawal amounts and per-route fees vary; CCTP "fast" transfers cost more than standard.
- Contract addresses on the CCTP doc page I read were the testnet ones — pull mainnet addresses from [docs.arc.io/arc/references/contract-addresses](https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/contract-addresses) before sending anything.

If you tell me which exchange or which chain you're coming from (e.g. Coinbase USDC on Base, or ETH on Ethereum), I can give you the exact click-path or the specific route with the lowest fee.
